commit.message:
fix: preserve account failover across SSE keepalives

Run streaming priority selection inside the client-facing response so headers and keepalives do not wait for an account verdict. Suppress eligible refusals only before content or tool exposure, join cancelled attempts before fallback, and bound the relay queue and undecided prelude.

Cover fragmented SSE bytes, reader cleanup, cancellation, terminal pool errors and a real socket heartbeat before delayed refusal. Add an installed-package probe with optional local fixtures while preserving the existing SDK idle guard and non-stream routing.
feat(session): add opt-in SQLite bookkeeping with offline recovery
Merge upstream/main into feat/sqlite-session-bookkeeping-public
chore(session): drop internal evidence notes and stray code
fix: keep pre-stream statuses and classify in-stream dispatch failures
chore(session): trim comments and name the unavailable-operation error plainly
Merge fix/sse-keepalive-failover into feat/sqlite-session-bookkeeping-public
ci: rerun after an unrelated /inflight timing flake

Merge upstream/main into feat/sqlite-session-bookkeeping-public

# Conflicts:
#	E2E.md
test(session): give the GC sweep harness the profile-copy pruning dependencies

Merge upstream/main into feat/sqlite-session-bookkeeping-public

Conflicts in package.json (test lists unioned), E2E.md (both sections kept) and
src/proxy/server.ts. Resolution notes:

- Upstream's terminal-publication deferral (097530c) applies in JSON mode only.
  In SQLite mode its mapping invalidation needs the same writer lock and
  lifecycle queue that refused the publication, and a failed invalidation of a
  resumed mapping keeps the session turn fence, so every retry of that
  conversation would hang. SQLite keeps its retryable fail-closed 503. The
  deferral is async because eviction is async on this branch.
- finalizePriorityPublication stays awaited, with upstream's enqueueTerminalDelta.
- closeBackend keeps the in-flight guard and also closes the auth-status owner
  (#1300); shutdown with requests still in flight closes that owner alone.
- startProxyServer keeps bookkeeping startup and builds the server with
  createProxyServerWithAuthOwner.
- The lifecycle queue reports to telemetry through a sink the server registers,
  so the bookkeeping CLI no longer opens the telemetry database on import.
test(session): a resumed SQLite turn refused by a held writer lock stays retryable

fix(session): treat a bootstrap seen mid-publication as busy

Two runtimes starting on a fresh directory race the bootstrap: the second sees
the published file with two links, then inspects aliases while the first one
removes its alias. The straddled scan reported an ambiguous hardlink, a plain
error that startup does not retry. Recheck the link count and report busy when
the publication moved during inspection, so startup retries.

fix: stop the model when a client cancels a priority-routed request

Under active+priority routing a client that went away before the first
byte of output never stopped the model: the SDK child ran on to the end
of its turn, on the account's allowance. That is Esc on a turn still
thinking, and an orchestrator cancelling subagents still queued for an
SDK slot or starting their CLI. A streaming client that had already read
bytes still stopped it by cancelling the body.

Every attempt of a priority-routed request adopts the request's abort
link (#1022), which hears the client go, the turn watchdog, a parent's
cancellation and shutdown. The handler's last finally detached the link
whether it had made it or adopted it. The priority dispatch returns from
inside that try, so the link was detached before the first attempt ran,
and each attempt's own return detached it again before the next. The
stream paths already detached only when the stream did not own the
link, which never held there; all three now detach a link only where it
was made. The outer handler still detaches the request's link once the
request is over.

priority-client-cancel.test.ts: a plain request, a streaming one before
its first byte, and one on the account a failover reached; each turn ran
its full length before and is stopped now.

scripts/e2e-claude-code-priority-cancel.mjs: the real client through the
built proxy under Node, as `npm run start` runs it, the SDK and the CLI,
against a scripted API holding the first byte 20 s, the client killed
once the SDK child's turn reached it. Before (48f7825): manual routing
closed the SDK child's request 1,524 ms after, active+priority left 2
open 20 s later. After: 1,514 ms and 28 ms. Under Bun @hono/node-server
is never told of a client gone before the first byte, in any mode.

Rebased onto current main: the source's hunks to
scripts/e2e-claude-code-parallel-subagents.mjs (a PROFILES knob) and
src/__tests__/account-return-trip.test.ts (the session-carry cancel
test) are left out; neither file exists on main, and both belong to
other parts of the source stack. The test's second profile id is a
placeholder, `spare`.

(cherry picked from commit e836030083bb1e62f630cdb953fe391a4b067ffb)

commit.message:
test: hold a priority-routed request to end at the cancel, and the watchdog to reach it

The source held "the request ends at the cancel" in the session-carry
test, which is not on main. That check now lives with the cancel cases:
each priority-routed cancel must also end the request within 1.5 s of
the cancel, against a 3 s turn.

Two more cases. The session-turn watchdog aborts through the same
request-wide link, so on main it could not stop a priority-routed turn
either; it does now. A manual-routing cancel is the control that already
passed on main, so a harness that could not cancel at all would fail it.

Mocked SDK, against the server of current main and of this branch:
main 1 pass / 4 fail (only the manual control passes; each priority
case runs its full 3 s turn), this branch 5 pass / 0 fail.

Also drops an issue number from the file's comment.

commit.message:
test: make the priority cancel gate fail on main through the session-turn watchdog

On current main a priority-routed stream sends its headers before an
account answers, so killing the real client is also seen by the
response body being cancelled: the gate's two client legs pass with and
without the fix, and no longer show the bug.

The watchdog reaches the SDK child only through the request's abort
link. Two new legs keep the client and let a 4 s session-turn watchdog
fire. Real client 2.1.301, built proxy under Node, scripted API:

  main (ca716c36)  manual 3,147 ms; active+priority 1 request still
                   open 20 s later (FAIL)
  this branch      manual 3,326 ms; active+priority 3,202 ms (PASS)

The client legs: main 1,487 / 1,484 ms, this branch 1,487 / 1,523 ms.

commit.message:
fix: take a moved conversation's session with it

Each account's SDK child keeps its sessions in that account's config
directory, and Meridian keeps a mapping of each conversation per account,
which a profile switch leaves in place. Back to an account it had used,
the conversation resumed the session it left there, and the turns it took
elsewhere went to that session as a resume delta, which keeps only the
user's side: with a mocked SDK the model was sent three questions in a
row, the two answers given on the other account gone.

An account now resumes its own copy only when no other account's copy
that holds the same history was used since (newestCopyElsewhere,
lineage reason moved-on-elsewhere). Otherwise the history is replayed.

Only the stale-copy guard is carved here; the transcript carry of the
source commit is left out.

Carved from commit 835cbf192cd6dc742ef29241724d2e2c988f8239.

commit.message:
fix: carry a conversation only from a copy that holds more of it

An account's own copy gave way to any copy elsewhere used more recently
whose lineage had not diverged. A rewind after a move and back broke on
that: the history the client sends is wholly inside the account's own
session, but the copy elsewhere, gone further, is an undo of it. It took
over and the whole history was replayed flattened.

A copy elsewhere now takes over only when it holds more of the history at
hand: a continuation or compaction holds what it resumes from and the
reply it wrote to that; an undo, all but the new message. Of several, the
one holding the most is taken, a continuation first.

Only the stale-copy guard's ranking (messagesHeld,
copyElsewhereHoldingMore) and its rewind test are carved here; the
transcript carry's last-turn wait, cancellation cleanup and file writing
are left out.

Carved from commit 48f782521901867b7dcd8a82a1d84efceadf2ecc.

commit.message:
fix: carry a conversation keyed by its fingerprint as one keyed by a session

A client that sends no session key (ForgeCode, Droid, a headerless Pi) is
kept under its conversation's fingerprint, scoped to each account as a
session key is. The stale-copy guard asked for a session key, so such a
conversation that came back to an account resumed the copy it left
there, and was sent the turns taken elsewhere as a resume delta without
the replies given there. The guard now finds the copies on other
accounts under the fingerprint those accounts keep it by.

account-return-trip.test.ts: the way back for a ForgeCode client (RED:
"SECOND-QUESTION ... THIRD-QUESTION ... FOURTH-QUESTION" sent to the
stale copy). The carry half of the source commit is left out.

commit.message:
fix(session): check other accounts' copies only when this account's would be resumed

The carved guard looked for a copy elsewhere also when this account had
none (lineage not-found), a case only the transcript carry used. Without
the carry that costs every new conversation one store read per other
account for nothing. Look only when the copy here would be resumed.

State how the guard sits on the raw-client/execution split: both copies
are measured against the raw client lineage, which decides ownership,
so a copy elsewhere published from a plugin-rewritten history (empty
lineageHash, raw clientLineageHash) still counts; the replay the guard
forces runs the execution history and publishes under the same
SDK-prefix proof rules as any other replay. Bring the profile-copy grace
comment in line: a copy left on an account is resumed only while no
other account's copy holds more of the history.

docs(session): state the moved-on-elsewhere rule and the control's limit precisely

The divergence reason's comment described the earlier rule (another
